title: Ensure dm-verity is configured
description: dm-verity provides transparent integrity checking of block devices using a cryptographic digest. Because dm-verity devices are read-only, filesystems mounted from the devices are also read-only. The audit requires dm-mod.create=root,,,ro,0, root=/dev/dm-0 and restart_on_corruption on /proc/cmdline. Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.1 Ensure dm-verity is configured

audit.command:
c=$(cat /proc/cmdline 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
bad=0
for w in 'dm-mod.create=root,,,ro,0' 'root=/dev/dm-0' restart_on_corruption; do
  printf '%s\n' "$c" | grep -Fwq -- "$w" || { echo "kernel cmdline lacks $w"; bad=1; }
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Replace the system or reinstall the distribution.

title: Ensure SELinux is configured
description: SELinux must be enabled and in enforcing mode. The audit runs sestatus and requires SELinux enabled with the fortified policy and enforcing current and configured mode (falls back to getenforce = Enforcing when sestatus is not present). Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.1 Ensure SELinux is configured

audit.command:
if command -v sestatus >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  out=$(sestatus 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
  bad=0
  for l in 'SELinux status: enabled' 'Loaded policy name: fortified' 'Current mode: enforcing' 'Mode from config file: enforcing'; do
    printf '%s\n' "$out" | tr -s ' \t' ' ' | grep -Fxq -- "$l" || { echo "missing: $l"; bad=1; }
  done
  [ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant
else
  m=$(getenforce 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
  [ "$m" = Enforcing ] && echo compliant || echo "SELinux: $m"
fi

remediation.guidance: Replace the system or reinstall the distribution.

title: Ensure the admin host container is disabled when not in use
description: The admin container is privileged and can obtain a root shell on the host (sheltie) and runs an SSH server. It should be enabled only for troubleshooting. The audit runs "apiclient get settings.host-containers.admin.enabled"; run it from the control container (for example via SSM: apiclient exec control ...), since running it inside the admin container proves the container is on and the rule will fail.
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark - Host containers / administrative access (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
out=$(apiclient get settings.host-containers.admin.enabled 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s' "$out" | tr -d ' \n' | sed -n 's/.*"enabled":\([a-z]*\).*/\1/p')
[ "$v" = false ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Set in user data: [settings.host-containers.admin] enabled = false, or after troubleshooting run from the control container: apiclient set host-containers.admin.enabled=false.

title: Ensure software update repositories are configured
description: Systems need to have software update repositories configured to ensure they receive the latest updates. Manual review against site policy.
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.1 Ensure software update repositories are configured

audit.command: Verify software update repositories are configured correctly. This command should display a list of available updates and return without error: # apiclient update check

remediation.command: Configure your software update repositories according to site policy.

title: Ensure setuid programs do not create core dumps
description: A core dump is the memory of an executable program. It is generally used to determine why a program aborted. It can also be used to glean confidential information from a core file. The audit reads /proc/sys/fs/suid_dumpable and requires 0. Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4.1 Ensure setuid programs do not create core dumps

audit.command:
bad=0
chk() { f=/proc/sys/$(printf %s "$1" | tr . /); v=$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$1: not readable"; bad=1; return; }; [ "$v" = "$2" ] || { echo "$1 = $v (expected $2)"; bad=1; }; }
chk fs.suid_dumpable 0
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to set the active kernel parameter and persist the setting: # apiclient apply <<EOF [settings.kernel.sysctl] "fs.suid_dumpable" = "0" EOF

title: Ensure chrony is configured
description: chrony is a daemon which implements the Network Time Protocol (NTP). It is designed to synchronize system clocks across a variety of systems and use a source that is highly accurate. The audit runs apiclient get settings.ntp.time-servers (at least one server) and systemctl is-active chronyd (active). Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.1.1 Ensure chrony is configured

audit.command:
out=$(apiclient get settings.ntp.time-servers 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s' "$out" | tr -d ' \n' | grep -Eq '"time-servers":\["[^"]+' || { echo 'no NTP time-servers configured'; exit 1; }
s=$(systemctl is-active chronyd 2>/dev/null)
[ "$s" = active ] && echo compliant || echo "chronyd: ${s:-unknown}"

remediation.guidance: Configure additional time servers as needed. The following command would add "2.pool.ntp.org" to the list of time servers. # apiclient apply <<EOF [settings.ntp] time-servers = [ "2.pool.ntp.org" ] EOF If chrony is not running, update to a version of the OS with the correct service configuration.

description: When tcp_syncookies is set, the kernel will handle TCP SYN packets normally until the half-open connection queue is full, at which time, the SYN cookie functionality kicks in. SYN cookies work by not using the SYN queue at all. The audit reads the running value from /proc/sys. Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).

title: Ensure journald is configured to write logs to persistent disk
description: Data from the journal may be stored in volatile memory or persisted locally on the server. Logs in memory will be lost upon a system reboot. By persisting logs to local disk on the server they are protected from loss. The audit requires Storage=persistent in /usr/lib/systemd/journald.conf.d/journald.conf. Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.1.1 Ensure journald is configured to write logs to persistent disk

audit.command:
f=/usr/lib/systemd/journald.conf.d/journald.conf
[ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*Storage=persistent[[:space:]]*$' "$f" && echo compliant || echo "Storage=persistent not set in $f"

remediation.guidance: Update to a version of the OS with the correct journald configuration.

title: Ensure permissions on journal files are configured
description: The journal is stored in /var/log/journal, and contains logged information from all services on the system. The audit lists files under /var/log/journal with group write/execute or any other permission and requires none. Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.2 Ensure permissions on journal files are configured

remediation.command: Run the following commands to set permissions on all existing log files: # find /var/log/journal -type f -perm /g+wx,o+rwx -exec chmod g-wx,o-rwx "{}" +

title: Ensure mounting of udf filesystems is disabled
description: The udf filesystem type is the universal disk format used to implement ISO/IEC 13346 and ECMA-167 specifications. This is an open vendor filesystem type for data storage on a broad range of media. This filesystem type is necessary to support writing DVDs and newer optical disc formats. The audit requires the udf module not to be loaded and blocked (modprobe -n -v shows install /bin/true, or apiclient settings.kernel.modules.udf.allowed is false). Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.1.1 Ensure mounting of udf filesystems is disabled

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to disable the udf module: # apiclient set kernel.modules.udf.allowed=false Run the following command to unload the udf module: # rmmod udf

title: Ensure packet redirect sending is disabled
description: ICMP Redirects are used to send routing information to other hosts. As a host itself does not act as a router (in a host only configuration), there is no need to send redirects. The audit reads the running values from /proc/sys. Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).

title: Ensure source routed packets are not accepted
description: In networking, source routing allows a sender to partially or fully specify the route packets take through a network. In contrast, non-source routed packets travel a path determined by routers in the network. In some cases, systems may not be routable or reachable from some locations (e.g. private addresses vs. The audit reads the running values from /proc/sys (IPv6 keys only when IPv6 is enabled). Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).

audit.command:
bad=0

title: Ensure SCTP is disabled
description: The Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) is a transport layer protocol used to support message oriented communication, with several streams of messages in one connection. It serves a similar function as TCP and UDP, incorporating features of both. It is message-oriented like UDP, and ensures reliable in-sequence transport of messages with congestion control like TCP. The audit requires the sctp module not to be loaded and blocked (modprobe -n -v shows install /bin/true, or apiclient settings.kernel.modules.sctp.allowed is false). Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.3.1 Ensure SCTP is disabled

title: Ensure IPv4 default deny firewall policy
description: A default deny all policy on connections ensures that any unconfigured network usage will be rejected. The audit runs iptables -L -n and requires DROP or REJECT policy on INPUT, FORWARD and OUTPUT. Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4.1.1 Ensure IPv4 default deny firewall policy

audit.command:
out=$(iptables -L -n 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
bad=0
for c in INPUT FORWARD OUTPUT; do
  p=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n "s/^Chain $c (policy \([A-Z]*\).*/\1/p")
  case "$p" in DROP|REJECT) ;; *) echo "$c policy ${p:-unknown}"; bad=1 ;; esac
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to implement a default DROP policy: # iptables -P INPUT DROP # iptables -P OUTPUT DROP # iptables -P FORWARD DROP

title: Ensure IPv4 loopback traffic is configured
description: Configure the loopback interface to accept traffic. Configure all other interfaces to deny traffic to the loopback network (127.0.0.0/8). The audit runs iptables -S and requires the INPUT lo ACCEPT, INPUT 127.0.0.0/8 DROP and OUTPUT lo ACCEPT rules (rule order is not verified). Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4.1.2 Ensure IPv4 loopback traffic is configured

remediation.command: Run the following commands to implement the loopback rules: # iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT # iptables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT # iptables -A INPUT -s 127.0.0.0/8 -j DROP

title: Ensure IPv4 outbound and established connections are configured

reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4.1.3 Ensure IPv4 outbound and established connections are configured

audit.command: Run the following command and verify all rules for new outbound, and established connections match site policy: # iptables -L -v -n

remediation.command: Configure iptables in accordance with site policy. The following commands will implement a policy to allow all outbound connections and all established connections: # iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # iptables -A OUTPUT -p udp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # iptables -A OUTPUT -p icmp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # iptables -A INPUT -p udp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # iptables -A INPUT -p icmp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to implement a default DROP policy: # ip6tables -P INPUT DROP # ip6tables -P OUTPUT DROP # ip6tables -P FORWARD DROP

title: Ensure IPv6 loopback traffic is configured
description: Configure the loopback interface to accept traffic. Configure all other interfaces to deny traffic to the loopback network (::1). The audit runs ip6tables -S and requires the INPUT lo ACCEPT, INPUT ::1 DROP and OUTPUT lo ACCEPT rules (rule order is not verified). Run tmaegis on the host through the admin container root shell (sudo sheltie).
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4.2.2 Ensure IPv6 loopback traffic is configured

remediation.command: Run the following commands to implement the loopback rules: # ip6tables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT # ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT # ip6tables -A INPUT -s ::1 -j DROP

title: Ensure IPv6 outbound and established connections are configured
description: Configure the firewall rules for new outbound, and established IPv6 connections. Manual review against site policy.
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4.2.3 Ensure IPv6 outbound and established connections are configured

audit.command: Run the following command and verify all rules for new outbound, and established connections match site policy: # ip6tables -L -v -n

remediation.command: Configure iptables in accordance with site policy. The following commands will implement a policy to allow all outbound connections and all established connections: # ip6tables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # ip6tables -A OUTPUT -p udp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # ip6tables -A OUTPUT -p icmp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # ip6tables -A INPUT -p tcp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # ip6tables -A INPUT -p udp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # ip6tables -A INPUT -p icmp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

title: Ensure access to the kernel log is restricted
description: kernel.dmesg_restrict=1 stops unprivileged processes (including containers) from reading kernel addresses and other sensitive data from dmesg. Bottlerocket /etc is ephemeral, so the value must be persisted through the API. The audit runs "apiclient get settings.kernel.sysctl" (from the admin container root shell or control container): if the API sets kernel.dmesg_restrict it must equal 1; if the API does not set it, the running value in /proc/sys must already equal 1.
reference: CIS Bottlerocket Benchmark - Kernel parameters / restrict dmesg access (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
out=$(apiclient get settings.kernel.sysctl 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s' "$out" | tr -d ' \n' | sed -n 's/.*"kernel\.dmesg_restrict":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
if [ -z "$v" ]; then v=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/dmesg_restrict 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; fi
[ "$v" = "1" ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Set in user data: [settings.kernel.sysctl] "kernel.dmesg_restrict" = "1", or at runtime: apiclient set --json '{"kernel":{"sysctl":{"kernel.dmesg_restrict":"1"}}}'
